A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S2O work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–D report original accuracy, sparsity, approximation-error, latency, ablation and attention-heatmap results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and reports additional controlled kernel-overhead experiments and matched-sparsity comparisons in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The segment ranking, index-guided loading, two-pass attention and early-stopping procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 match; the new kernel controls do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: InfiniteBench, RULER and LongBench v2 coverage is retained, as are causal and non-causal attention settings. The new kernel studies change experimental controls rather than task coverage. V2 mentions forthcoming DiT analysis but supplies no corresponding evaluation.

E2.justification: The main Full, FlexPrefill, XAttn and PBS comparator set is unchanged. Appendix B adds a comparison against a method labeled BSA and replaces the earlier permutation-style comparison with dense, indexed-sequential, indexed-sorted and early-stop controls.

E3.justification: Appendix B substantially redesigns the overhead evaluation: the two-device, 128K non-causal Triton comparison becomes an A100 study using controlled FlashAttention-2 derivatives across 8K–128K and both masking modes. Threshold −1 enforces equal computation, and a separate TopK experiment matches sparsity at 32K and 128K. Main benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the earlier aggregate overhead comparison with an ABCD decomposition isolating indexing, non-contiguous access and early-stop control costs. New Figure 6 tests whether comparable sparsity produces comparable runtime against BSA. Existing hyperparameter/component ablations and qualitative heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean latency over unspecified multiple post-warmup iterations and mention shared random seeds where applicable. V2 adds no run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Changes are confined to supporting kernel results and Figure 1. New Tables 4–6 report component latencies and roughly 13–16% total overhead under revised conditions; Figure 6 adds BSA comparison curves. Retained benchmark tables and Figure 5 are numerically unchanged. Figure 1 switches XAttn/PBS speedups from 3.00×/2.74× to 2.74×/3.00×, conflicting with retained Figure 5c.

T1.justification: The ranking definitions, Equations 1–2 and retrieval-complexity discussion are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: overcoming block-granularity redundancy through online permutation and early stopping. Their headline accuracy, sparsity and speedup claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds component-specific explanations of overhead and interprets the BSA comparison as evidence that finer-grained sparsity remains practical. It removes the explicit limitations concerning hyperparameter transfer, decoder-only prefill scope, untested architectures/training, and hardware/software generalization.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds benchmark-specific kernel provenance, cp_async indexed-loading details, deferred early-stop checking, shared kernel configurations, and settings including batch size 1 and segment length 1024. These document the new controlled experiments; the main S2O defaults remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 32 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Expanded author lists, additional bibliographic metadata and numbered citations do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: Most retained prose is unchanged. V2 expands Appendix B and Figure 3's caption, reorganizes Appendix C into separate experimental subsections, removes the limitations section, and changes citation and author-header formatting.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different template with a branded header, full-width boxed abstract and revised typography. Figure 1 is redrawn using relative-time bars; the overhead table is replaced by three tables and a new figure. Existing tables move, and the retained appendix heatmaps occupy separate pages.

improvement.justification: The controlled decomposition and matched-sparsity comparison strengthen the overhead evidence beyond v1's comparison of different kernel implementations. However, v2 removes substantive applicability limitations and introduces inconsistent XAttn/PBS speedups in Figure 1. With the main method and benchmark results unchanged, these competing gains and reporting losses do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
